</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Before proving <a href="#Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2. ‣ B.2 Dual form ‣ Appendix B Derivation of BFE-W ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, we require a lemma on factorization of pseudo-determinants.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3</span></span><span id="Thmlemma3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Pseudo-Determinant Factorization)<span id="Thmlemma3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{B}}\in\real^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{A}},{\mathbf{B}}\in\real^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> be symmetric positive semi-definite matrices with <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\textnormal{Rank}}({\mathbf{A}})={\textnormal{Rank}}({\mathbf{B}})=c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Rank</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Rank</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\textnormal{Rank}}({\mathbf{A}})={\textnormal{Rank}}({\mathbf{B}})=c</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{A}})={\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{B}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Range</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Range</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{A}})={\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{B}})</annotation></semantics></math>. Then,</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx22" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex27"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}})={\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}){\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{B}})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>pdet</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>pdet</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>pdet</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}})={\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}){\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{B}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Take the compact spectral decompositions</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx23" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex28"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\mathbf{A}}={\mathbf{U}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{U}}^{T},\qquad{\mathbf{B}}={\mathbf{V}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}{\mathbf{V}}^{T}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐀</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐔</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐀</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐔</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐁</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐕</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐁</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐕</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\mathbf{A}}={\mathbf{U}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{U}}^{T},\qquad{\mathbf{B}}={\mathbf{V}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}{\mathbf{V}}^{T},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathbf{U}},{\mathbf{V}}\in\real^{d\times c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐔</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐕</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{U}},{\mathbf{V}}\in\real^{d\times c}</annotation></semantics></math> have orthonormal columns, and <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}},\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}\in\real^{c\times c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>𝐀</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>𝐁</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}},\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}\in\real^{c\times c}</annotation></semantics></math> are diagonal matrices containing the non-zero eigenvalues of <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{A}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{A}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{B}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{B}}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Since <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{A}})={\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{B}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Range</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Range</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{A}})={\textnormal{Range}}({\mathbf{B}})</annotation></semantics></math>, the columns of <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{U}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐔</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{U}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐕</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{V}}</annotation></semantics></math> are orthonormal bases for the same subspace. Hence, there exists an orthogonal <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathbf{R}}\in\real^{c\times c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐑</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{R}}\in\real^{c\times c}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{U}}={\mathbf{V}}{\mathbf{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐔</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐕𝐑</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{U}}={\mathbf{V}}{\mathbf{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore,</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx24" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex29"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}}={\mathbf{V}}{\mathbf{R}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{R}}^{T}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}{\mathbf{V}}^{T}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐀𝐁</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐕𝐑</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐀</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐁</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐕</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}}={\mathbf{V}}{\mathbf{R}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{R}}^{T}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}{\mathbf{V}}^{T}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p4.3.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{R}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{R}}^{T}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐑</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐀</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐁</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{R}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{R}}^{T}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is non-singular, its eigenvalues
are precisely the non-zero eigenvalues of <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐀𝐁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus,</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx25" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex30"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle{\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}})=\det({\mathbf{R}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{R}}^{T}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}})=\det({\mathbf{R}})^{2}\det(\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}})\det(\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}})={\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}){\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{B}})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>pdet</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐑</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐀</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐁</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐀</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>𝐁</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>pdet</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>pdet</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle{\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}{\mathbf{B}})=\det({\mathbf{R}}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}}{\mathbf{R}}^{T}\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}})=\det({\mathbf{R}})^{2}\det(\Lambda_{{\mathbf{A}}})\det(\Lambda_{{\mathbf{B}}})={\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{A}}){\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{B}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p4.4.1" class="ltx_text">where we used <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det({\mathbf{R}})^{2}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">det</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det({\mathbf{R}})^{2}=1</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We now prove the dual expansion of <a href="#S3.E2" title="In 3.1 Optimal features under interpolation for ridge regression ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of <a href="#Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2. ‣ B.2 Dual form ‣ Appendix B Derivation of BFE-W ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Under the rank and interpolation assumptions, <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{W}}=\Phi^{\dagger}{\mathbf{Y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>†</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{W}}=\Phi^{\dagger}{\mathbf{Y}}</annotation></semantics></math> is equivalent to <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi={\mathbf{Y}}{\mathbf{W}}^{\dagger}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝐘𝐖</mi><mo>†</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi={\mathbf{Y}}{\mathbf{W}}^{\dagger}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Range}({\mathbf{Y}}^{T}{\mathbf{Y}})=\text{Range}({\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Range</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐘</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Range</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Range}({\mathbf{Y}}^{T}{\mathbf{Y}})=\text{Range}({\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}})</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu=\lambda_{m}\tau_{m}/2=\tau/2\sigma^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu=\lambda_{m}\tau_{m}/2=\tau/2\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. We consider the trace and log-determinant terms in <a href="#S3.E2" title="In 3.1 Optimal features under interpolation for ridge regression ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> separately.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">Combining these terms, we get the following asymptotic expansion for <a href="#S3.E2" title="In 3.1 Optimal features under interpolation for ridge regression ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, for <math id="A2.SS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\to 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\to 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, evaluated using the weights</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx29" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex36"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex36.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{1}{nm}\mathcal{F}_{n}^{\tau_{m},\lambda_{m}}(\Phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{1}{nm}\mathcal{F}_{n}^{\tau_{m},\lambda_{m}}(\Phi)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex36.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda_{m}}{2n}{\textnormal{Tr}}({\mathbf{W}}{\mathbf{W}}^{T})-\frac{1}{2n}\log{\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{W}}{\mathbf{W}}^{T})+\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{2\pi}{\lambda_{m}m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>Tr</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mtext>pdet</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda_{m}}{2n}{\textnormal{Tr}}({\mathbf{W}}{\mathbf{W}}^{T})-\frac{1}{2n}\log{\textnormal{pdet}}({\mathbf{W}}{\mathbf{W}}^{T})+\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{2\pi}{\lambda_{m}m}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A2.SS2.p9.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p9.2.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Note that unlike the primal formulation, we cannot easily compare the dual expansion across models with differing <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>. For models trained on the same dataset, with the same final activation dimension <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, and full-rank features (i.e., <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=d_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=d_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>), taking the difference of the asymptotic expansions in <a href="#Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2. ‣ B.2 Dual form ‣ Appendix B Derivation of BFE-W ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, and then re-normalizing by <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, will result in the following <span id="A2.SS2.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">relative dual free energy:</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A2.SS2.p11.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="32" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 32" width="477.38"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,32) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#404040;" fill="#404040" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.91 L 0 26.09 C 0 29.36 2.64 32 5.91 32 L 471.47 32 C 474.73 32 477.38 29.36 477.38 26.09 L 477.38 5.91 C 477.38 2.64 474.73 0 471.47 0 L 5.91 0 C 2.64 0 0 2.64 0 5.91 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#F2F2F2;" fill="#F2F2F2" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.97 5.91 L 1.97 26.09 C 1.97 28.27 3.73 30.03 5.91 30.03 L 471.47 30.03 C 473.65 30.03 475.41 28.27 475.41 26.09 L 475.41 5.91 C 475.41 3.73 473.65 1.97 471.47 1.97 L 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 18.22)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:31.37em;--ltx-fo-height:0em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.32em;font-size:10pt;" height="4.44" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)" width="434.07"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

</span>

</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p12.1" class="ltx_p">However, in <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, we see that even for models with <span id="A2.SS2.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">different</span> activation dimension <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, this dual free energy shows strong correlation with model quality, for models in the Pythia suite of LLMs and the Qwen3.5 suite. Deriving an asymptotic expansion that allows for direct comparison across models with differing activation dimension is left for future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we give details on the HTMP distribution <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hodgkinson et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Take a random matrix <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> with beta-Laguerre ensemble of size <math id="A3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times N</annotation></semantics></math>, defined by its joint eigenvalue density function</p>
<table id="A3.EGx31" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.E4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle q(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{N})\propto\prod_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_{i}^{\frac{\tilde{\beta}}{2}(D-N+1)-1}e^{-\frac{\tilde{\beta}D}{2}\lambda_{i}}\prod_{i,j=1,\dots,N,~i&lt;j}|\lambda_{j}-\lambda_{i}|^{\tilde{\beta}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msubsup><mi>λ</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo rspace="0.437em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle q(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{N})\propto\prod_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_{i}^{\frac{\tilde{\beta}}{2}(D-N+1)-1}e^{-\frac{\tilde{\beta}D}{2}\lambda_{i}}\prod_{i,j=1,\dots,N,~i&lt;j}|\lambda_{j}-\lambda_{i}|^{\tilde{\beta}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">for some <math id="A3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\beta}=\tilde{\beta}(N)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\beta}=\tilde{\beta}(N)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D,N\in\mathbb{N}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D,N\in\mathbb{N},</annotation></semantics></math>where <math id="A3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=D(N)\geq N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=D(N)\geq N</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=\kappa(N)=\tilde{\beta}(N)N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=\kappa(N)=\tilde{\beta}(N)N</annotation></semantics></math>. As the ensemble size <math id="A3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, the empirical spectral distribution (ESD) of <math id="A3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> will converge to either the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) distribution, or the HTMP distribution, depending on the limit of <math id="A3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\beta}(N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\beta}(N)</annotation></semantics></math>. We first consider the case when <math id="A3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\beta}(N)N\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\beta}(N)N\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> (equivalently <math id="A3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa(N)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa(N)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>), where the ESD of <math id="A3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> converges to the MP distribution, with probability density function</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A3.EGx32" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex39"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\rho_{\gamma}(x)=(1-\gamma^{-1})^{+}\delta_{0}(x)+\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{\sqrt{(\gamma_{+}-x)^{+}(x-\gamma_{-})^{+}}}{\gamma x},\quad x\geq 0," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mo>−</mo></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></msqrt><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\rho_{\gamma}(x)=(1-\gamma^{-1})^{+}\delta_{0}(x)+\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{\sqrt{(\gamma_{+}-x)^{+}(x-\gamma_{-})^{+}}}{\gamma x},\quad x\geq 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(<span id="A3.Ex39.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MP</span>)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{\pm}=(1\pm\sqrt{\gamma})^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mo>±</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mi>γ</mi></msqrt></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{\pm}=(1\pm\sqrt{\gamma})^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x)^{+}=\max(0,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x)^{+}=\max(0,x)</annotation></semantics></math>. In this case, we have the following result.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hodgkinson et al. (2025)</a></cite>)<span id="Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\beta}(N)N\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\beta}(N)N\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N/D\to\gamma\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N/D\to\gamma\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, then the ESD <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> of beta-Laguerre ensemble <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, defined by <a href="#A3.E4" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, converges weakly to the Marchenko-Pastur distribution <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">MP</mtext><mi>γ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>, whose probability density function is <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\gamma}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\gamma}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> with parameter <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, defined in <a href="#A3.Ex39" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">MP</span></a>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If, instead, the temperature <math id="A3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\beta}(N)\sim\kappa/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\beta}(N)\sim\kappa/N</annotation></semantics></math>, then we arise at the high-temperature MP distribution, as stated in the following result.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 5</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hodgkinson et al. (2025)</a></cite>)<span id="Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa(N)=\tilde{\beta}(N)N\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa(N)=\tilde{\beta}(N)N\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N/D\to\gamma\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N/D\to\gamma\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, then the ESD <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> of beta-Laguerre ensemble <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, defined by <a href="#A3.E4" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, converges weakly to a probability distribution on <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,\infty)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,\infty)</annotation></semantics></math> with probability density function <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\gamma,\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\gamma,\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math> defined as</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx33" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex40"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex40.m1" class="ltx_Math" <p id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(a,b,z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(a,b,z)</annotation></semantics></math> is the Tricomi confluent hypergeometric function <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">DLMF, </a>)</cite>. This limiting spectrum is the <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">HTMP</mtext><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math> distribution, with parameter <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa,\gamma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa,\gamma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmremark3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 3</span></span><span id="Thmremark3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmremark3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hodgkinson et al. (2025, Theorem E.1)</a></cite>, <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{HTMP}_{\kappa,\gamma,\beta}\to\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">HTMP</mtext><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">MP</mtext><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{HTMP}_{\kappa,\gamma,\beta}\to\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa,\beta\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa,\beta\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa/\beta\to 2\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa/\beta\to 2\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.
This—coupled with the fact that the model can exhibit heavy-tailed ESDs, while not exhibiting heavy-tailed elements—means that the <math id="Thmremark3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{HTMP}_{\kappa,\gamma,\beta,\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">HTMP</mtext><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{HTMP}_{\kappa,\gamma,\beta,\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> distribution should well-model most stages of DNN training.<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note"><span id="footnote4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright">4</span></span>
                
                
                
                
                
                
                
              <span id="footnote4.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright">It will not cover bulk </span><math id="footnote4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math><span id="footnote4.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> spike distributions common for older DNNs; see </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Martin and Mahoney (2021)</a></cite><span id="footnote4.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> for the 5+1 phases.</span></span></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The Stieltjes transform of a probability distribution <math id="A3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is given by <math id="A3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\rho}(z)=\int(x-z)^{-1}\rho(x)dx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>ρ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\rho}(z)=\int(x-z)^{-1}\rho(x)dx</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the <math id="A3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">HTMP</mtext><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math> distribution <math id="A3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\gamma,\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\gamma,\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math>, the <span id="A3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stieltjes transform</span> is given by a result from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ismail et al. (1988)</a></cite>, as follows:</p>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Derivation of CDF for HTMP</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now derive the cumulative distribution function (CDF) for <a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4</span></span><span id="Thmlemma4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(CDF HTMP)<span id="Thmlemma4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The CDF for the density function <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx37" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex43"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)=\begin{cases}0,&amp;x&lt;0,\\
\frac{2}{\pi\kappa}\lim_{y\downarrow 0}{\textnormal{Arg}}_{\text{cont}}U\left(\frac{\kappa}{2},1-\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}+\frac{\kappa}{2};-\beta x-i\beta y\right),&amp;x\geq 0,\end{cases}" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mtext>Arg</mtext><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">cont</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)=\begin{cases}0,&amp;x&lt;0,\\
\frac{2}{\pi\kappa}\lim_{y\downarrow 0}{\textnormal{Arg}}_{\text{cont}}U\left(\frac{\kappa}{2},1-\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}+\frac{\kappa}{2};-\beta x-i\beta y\right),&amp;x\geq 0,\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmlemma4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\textnormal{Arg}}_{\text{cont}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext>Arg</mtext><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">cont</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\textnormal{Arg}}_{\text{cont}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the continuous, unwrapped argument, and <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\textnormal{Arg}}_{\text{cont}}(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>Arg</mtext><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">cont</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\textnormal{Arg}}_{\text{cont}}(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=\kappa/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=\kappa/2</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b=1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b=1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}(z)=a^{-1}\partial_{z}\log U(a,b,-\beta z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∂</mo><mi>z</mi></msub><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}(z)=a^{-1}\partial_{z}\log U(a,b,-\beta z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Now we can write the CDF through the Stieltjes inversion formula <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib85" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai, 1999</a>, Eq. 3.2)</cite>,</span></p>

0}\int_{0}^{x}\Im S_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(t+iy)dt=\frac{1}{\pi a}\lim_{y\downarrow 0}\int_{0}^{x}\Im[\partial_{t}\log U(a,b,-\beta(t+iy))]dt." display="inline" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>x</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℑ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)-F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(0)=\frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{y\downarrow 0}\int_{0}^{x}\Im S_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(t+iy)dt=\frac{1}{\pi a}\lim_{y\downarrow <p id="A3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">As <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is supported on <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(0)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(0)=0</annotation></semantics></math>. We write <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(a,b;z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(a,b;z)</annotation></semantics></math> in its polar form, <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(a,b;z)=R(x)\exp(i\Theta(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(a,b;z)=R(x)\exp(i\Theta(x))</annotation></semantics></math>, where we take <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta(x)</annotation></semantics></math> as the continuous argument. We can then write</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">Hence,</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="A3.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">Now, <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U(a,b;-iy)=\Gamma(1-b)/\Gamma(a-b+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U(a,b;-iy)=\Gamma(1-b)/\Gamma(a-b+1)</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">DLMF, </a>)</cite>. For <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=\kappa/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=\kappa/2</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b=1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b=1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-b&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-b&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a-b+1&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a-b+1&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, hence, <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U(a,b;-iy)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U(a,b;-iy)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{y\downarrow 0}\Theta(0-i\beta y)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{y\downarrow 0}\Theta(0-i\beta y)=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus,</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx41" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex47"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)=\frac{1}{\pi a}\lim_{y\downarrow 0}\Theta(-\beta x-i\beta y)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle F_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(x)=\frac{1}{\pi a}\lim_{y\downarrow 0}\Theta(-\beta x-i\beta y).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Now, in <a href="#A7.SS2" title="G.2 Fitting the HTMP ‣ Appendix G Experimental details ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G.2</span></a> we discuss fitting the HTMP by minimizing Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance, i.e. by minimizing the pointwise supremum of the HTMP CDF to the empirical CDF. To do this efficiently, it will be useful to be able to compute the <span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">principal</span> argument of <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U\left(\kappa/2,1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2;-\beta x-i\beta y\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U\left(\kappa/2,1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2;-\beta x-i\beta y\right)</annotation></semantics></math>; then, an unwrapping process on a grid of inputs <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> will return the continuous argument. Hence, we present the following result, which provides the real and imaginary parts of <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U\left(\kappa/2,1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2;-\beta x-i\beta y\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{y\downarrow 0}U\left(\kappa/2,1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2;-\beta x-i\beta y\right)</annotation></semantics></math>; further, these parts only involve functions that can be easily computed numerically (i.e. they do not require complex arguments). However, note that this form only holds when <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\kappa/2\gamma+\kappa/2</annotation></semantics></math> is not an integer.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5</span></span><span id="Thmlemma5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Non-Integer Evaluation of HTMP CDF)<span id="Thmlemma5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(a,b,x)={}_{1}F_{1}(a,b,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>F</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><mn>1</mn><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(a,b,x)={}_{1}F_{1}(a,b,x)</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b\notin\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b\notin\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx42" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="A3.SS1.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">By Kummer’s transformation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">DLMF, </a>, Eq. 13.2.42)</cite>, we can write</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Kummer’s function <math id="A3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M(a,b,z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(a,b,z)</annotation></semantics></math> is entire <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">DLMF, </a>, §13.2)</cite>; further, letting <math id="A3.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Log}(z)=\log|z|+i\arg(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>Log</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Log}(z)=\log|z|+i\arg(z)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the principal logarithm,</span></p>
