</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Derivation of limiting free energy</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we will derive the limiting expression of <a href="#S3.Ex4" title="In 3.2 Evaluation of free energy using final-layer weights ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">BFE-
                              
                                W
                              
                            </span></a>, as given in <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2. ‣ 4.2 Limiting free energy ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. We will assume weights <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathbf{W}}_{l}\in\real^{d_{l-1}\times d_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{W}}_{l}\in\real^{d_{l-1}\times d_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math>, that follow <a href="#Thmassumption2" title="Assumption 2. ‣ 4.1 Trained weight spectra ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Assumption</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. Further, as this assumption only gives weak convergence, we require the following integrability assumptions.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmassumption4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmassumption4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 4</span></span><span id="Thmassumption4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Uniform Integrability)<span id="Thmassumption4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmassumption4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmassumption4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmassumption4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume <math id="Thmassumption4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{d_{l}}d_{l}^{-1}{\textnormal{Tr}}\left(\left({\mathbf{W}}_{l}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}_{l}\right)^{1+\epsilon}\right)&lt;\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>sup</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>Tr</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{d_{l}}d_{l}^{-1}{\textnormal{Tr}}\left(\left({\mathbf{W}}_{l}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}_{l}\right)^{1+\epsilon}\right)&lt;\infty</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="Thmassumption4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmassumption5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmassumption5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption 5</span></span><span id="Thmassumption5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Logarithmic Integrability)<span id="Thmassumption5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmassumption5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmassumption5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmassumption5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Denote <math id="Thmassumption5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\rho}_{d_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\rho}_{d_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math> as the ESD for <math id="Thmassumption5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{W}}_{l}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{W}}_{l}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, assume</span></p>
<table id="A4.EGx47" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.Ex57"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex57.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\lim_{\delta\to 0^{+}}~\underset{d_{l}\to\infty}{\lim\sup}\int_{0}^{\delta}|\log x|d\bar{\rho}_{d_{l}}(x)=0." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo lspace="0.497em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.0835em">lim</mo><mo lspace="0.0835em" movablelimits="false">sup</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.700em">d</mi><mi mathsize="0.710em">l</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.700em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathsize="0.700em" mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>δ</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\lim_{\delta\to 0^{+}}~\underset{d_{l}\to\infty}{\lim\sup}\int_{0}^{\delta}|\log x|d\bar{\rho}_{d_{l}}(x)=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Note that <a href="#Thmassumption4" title="Assumption 4 (Uniform Integrability). ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Assumption</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> is a standard moment assumption in RMT. For <a href="#Thmassumption5" title="Assumption 5 (Logarithmic Integrability). ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Assumption</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, this controls the convergence of <math id="A4.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\log\det({\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\det({\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}})</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Both assumptions are valid for non-degenerate Wishart matrices.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To derive the limiting expression for <math id="A4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{d_{l}}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{d_{l}}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we require the limiting expressions for <math id="A4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m^{-1}{\textnormal{Tr}}{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>Tr</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m^{-1}{\textnormal{Tr}}{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m^{-1}\log\det{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">det</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m^{-1}\log\det{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. These terms relate to the first moment and the Shannon transform of <a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Shannon transform</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The limiting log-determinant of <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}</annotation></semantics></math>, under our spectral assumptions, is given by the Shannon transform of <a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>. We now derive this.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefinition2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefinition2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefinition2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Shannon transform of distribution <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is given by <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{\rho}(x):={\mathbb{E}}_{\lambda\sim\rho}\left[\log\left(\frac{\lambda}{x}+1\right)\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>ρ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{\rho}(x):={\mathbb{E}}_{\lambda\sim\rho}\left[\log\left(\frac{\lambda}{x}+1\right)\right]</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tulino and Verdú, 2004</a>)</cite>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 6</span></span><span id="Thmlemma6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Derivation of Shannon Transform for HTMP)<span id="Thmlemma6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Shannon transform <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</span></p>
<table id="A4.EGx48" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="A4.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We have the following identity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tulino and Verdú, 2004</a>)</cite>:</span></p>
<table id="A4.EGx50" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.E6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}(x)=\int_{0}^{\infty}\log\left(1+\frac{\lambda}{x}\right)\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(d\lambda)=\int_{x}^{+\infty}\left(\frac{1}{z}-S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}(-z)\right)dz." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>z</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mover stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">To compute the Shannon transform, we require the anti-derivative of the integrand in the final expression in <a href="#A4.E6" title="In Proof. ‣ D.1 Shannon transform ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, i.e., some function <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}^{\prime}(z)=z^{-1}-S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}(-z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}^{\prime}(z)=z^{-1}-S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}(-z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{z}U(a,b,z)=-aU(a+1,b+1,z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>z</mi></msub><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{z}U(a,b,z)=-aU(a+1,b+1,z)</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">DLMF, </a>)</cite>. From this, we can write the Stieltjes transform as follows:</span></p>

<p id="A4.SS1.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text">We now need to consider the asymptotics of <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>, to compute the integral in <a href="#A4.E6" title="In Proof. ‣ D.1 Shannon transform ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>. Note from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">DLMF ()</a></cite>, <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|U(a,b,z)|\sim|z|^{-a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|U(a,b,z)|\sim|z|^{-a}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|z|\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|z|\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\arg z|&lt;3\pi/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\arg z|&lt;3\pi/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence,</span></p>

<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>First and second moments</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The limiting trace of <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{W}}^{T}{\mathbf{W}}</annotation></semantics></math>, under our spectral assumptions, is given by the first moment of <a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>. We derive this now (as well as the second moment).</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 7</span></span><span id="Thmlemma7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(First and Second Moment)<span id="Thmlemma7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Denoting <math id="Thmlemma7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> as the <math id="Thmlemma7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k^{\text{th}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>k</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">th</mtext></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^{\text{th}}</annotation></semantics></math> moment of the <math id="Thmlemma7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">HTMP</mtext><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> distribution, i.e., <math id="Thmlemma7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{k}=\int\lambda^{k}\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(d\lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∫</mo><mrow><msup><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{k}=\int\lambda^{k}\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}(d\lambda)</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A4.EGx57" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.Ex69"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex69.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mu_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mu_{1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex69.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma\beta},\quad\mu_{2}=\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma\beta^{2}}\cdot\left(\frac{\kappa(1+\gamma)}{2\gamma}+1\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma\beta},\quad\mu_{2}=\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma\beta^{2}}\cdot\left(\frac{\kappa(1+\gamma)}{2\gamma}+1\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of <a href="#Thmlemma7" title="Lemma 7 (First and Second Moment). ‣ D.2 First and second moments ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For probability measures <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> with finite first and second moments, <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have the following expansion of the Stieltjes transform, for argument <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\to-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\to-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mingo and Speicher, 2017</a>)</cite>,</span></p>
<table id="A4.EGx58" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.Ex70"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex70.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle S_{\nu}(z)=-z^{-1}-m_{1}z^{-2}-m_{2}z^{-3}+o(|z|^{-3})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle S_{\nu}(z)=-z^{-1}-m_{1}z^{-2}-m_{2}z^{-3}+o(|z|^{-3}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Hence, for <a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>, the first and second moments <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> are given by</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">An application of <a href="#Thmlemma11" title="Lemma 11. ‣ E.4 Auxiliary lemma ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> then gives the result.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Having derived the limiting deterministic quantity for <a href="#S3.Ex4" title="In 3.2 Evaluation of free energy using final-layer weights ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">BFE-
                              
                                W
                              
                            </span></a>, under <a href="#Thmassumption2" title="Assumption 2. ‣ 4.1 Trained weight spectra ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Assumption</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <a href="#Thmassumption4" title="Assumption 4 (Uniform Integrability). ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Assumption</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, <a href="#Thmassumption5" title="Assumption 5 (Logarithmic Integrability). ‣ Appendix D Derivation of limiting free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Assumption</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, we now provide various results and proofs on the behaviour of <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. This section will culminate with the proof of <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3. ‣ 4.2 Limiting free energy ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Optimality of free energy under ratio</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here, we give various results for the case when we are either controlling <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(\kappa)=\kappa/\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(\kappa)=\kappa/\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, for some given <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, or optimizing <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> after <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(\kappa)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(\kappa)</annotation></semantics></math> has attained its optima. In the general case (<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>), we are able to show that the Shannon transform is strictly increasing in <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>; trivially, the first moment is also strictly increasing in <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 8</span></span><span id="Thmlemma8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Increasing Shannon Transform)<span id="Thmlemma8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For fixed <math id="Thmlemma8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, the Shannon transform for <a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>, <math id="Thmlemma8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}</annotation></semantics></math>, is strictly increasing in <math id="Thmlemma8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Under the chain rule,</span></p>
<table id="A5.EGx61" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex74"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex74.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{V}}{\partial h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{V}}{\partial h}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex74.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\partial\mathcal{V}}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial\beta}{\partial h}=-\frac{\beta^{2}}{\kappa}\frac{\partial\mathcal{V}}{\partial\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>κ</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\partial\mathcal{V}}{\partial\beta}\frac{\partial\beta}{\partial h}=-\frac{\beta^{2}}{\kappa}\frac{\partial\mathcal{V}}{\partial\beta}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A5.Ex75"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A5.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Now, as <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the Stieltjes transform of a normalized probability distribution (<a href="#A3.Ex42" title="In Appendix C High-Temperature Marchenko-Pastur distribution ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">HTMP</span></a>), then for <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="xS_{\bar{\rho}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}}(-x)-1=\int x(\lambda+|x|)^{-1}d\rho(\lambda)-\int d\rho(\lambda)=-\int\lambda(\lambda+|x|)^{-1}d\rho(\lambda)&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mover stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mo>∫</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo rspace="0em">+</mo><mo fence="false" d\rho(\lambda)=-\int\lambda(\lambda+|x|)^{-1}d\rho(\lambda)&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math> for non-degenerate <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" Hence,</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">and <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{\bar{\rho}}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly increasing in <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(\kappa)=\kappa/\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(\kappa)=\kappa/\beta</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If we take minimum eigenvalue <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, then we can also show that for fixed <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, an optimal ratio <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> exists. To show this, we show strict convexity and coercivity of <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then derive the optimal <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 9</span></span><span id="Thmlemma9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Strict Convexity, Coercivity and Optimality of <math id="Thmlemma9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math>)<span id="Thmlemma9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For fixed <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly convex and coercive in <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>. Further, <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is minimized at <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}(\kappa)=2\gamma/\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}(\kappa)=2\gamma/\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>; equivalently <math id="Thmlemma9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{*}(\kappa)=\kappa\lambda/2\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta^{*}(\kappa)=\kappa\lambda/2\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
