<p id="A5.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Strict convexity is immediate by seeing that</span></p>
<table id="A5.EGx64" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex79"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex79.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\partial_{hh}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=\frac{1}{2h^{2}}&gt;0." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.167em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\partial_{hh}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=\frac{1}{2h^{2}}&gt;0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p4.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p4.3.1" class="ltx_text">To see coercivity, note that for <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\sim-\frac{1}{2}\log h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\sim-\frac{1}{2}\log h</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{h\to 0}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h\to 0}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Further, for <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\sim(\lambda/4\gamma)h-\frac{1}{2}\log h\sim(\lambda/4\gamma)h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\sim(\lambda/4\gamma)h-\frac{1}{2}\log h\sim(\lambda/4\gamma)h</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence, <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{h\to\infty}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{h\to\infty}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is coercive in <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly convex and coercive, a unique minimum <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> exists. Then,</span></p>
<table id="A5.EGx65" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex80"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex80.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\partial_{h}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}|_{h=h^{*}}=\frac{\lambda}{4\gamma}-\frac{1}{2h^{*}}=0," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>h</mi></msub><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.167em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><msub><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\partial_{h}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}|_{h=h^{*}}=\frac{\lambda}{4\gamma}-\frac{1}{2h^{*}}=0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p4.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p4.4.1" class="ltx_text">giving <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}(\kappa)=2\gamma/\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}(\kappa)=2\gamma/\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>, or equivalently <math id="A5.SS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{*}(\kappa)=\kappa\lambda/2\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta^{*}(\kappa)=\kappa\lambda/2\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Thus, for a fixed <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, an optimal <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> parameter exists (given as a ratio <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}=\kappa/\beta^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}=\kappa/\beta^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>). We are now interested in seeing how <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> behaves in <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="A5.SS1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> that follows the optimal ratio manifold. As we will see, the behavior is surprisingly simple.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 10</span></span><span id="Thmlemma10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">At <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta^{*}(\kappa)=\lambda\kappa/2\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta^{*}(\kappa)=\lambda\kappa/2\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly decreasing in <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">We take the derivative of <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A5.EGx66" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex81"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex81.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\kappa^{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial\kappa}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>κ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\kappa^{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial\kappa}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex81.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\kappa(1-\gamma)}{2\gamma}\psi\left(\frac{\kappa(1-\gamma)}{2\gamma}\right)-\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}\psi\left(\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\kappa(1-\gamma)}{2\gamma}\psi\left(\frac{\kappa(1-\gamma)}{2\gamma}\right)-\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}\psi\left(\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A5.Ex82"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex82.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle-\log\Gamma\left(\kappa(1-\gamma)/2\gamma\right)+\log\Gamma\left(\kappa/2\gamma\right)-\frac{\kappa(1-\gamma)}{2\gamma}+\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle-\log\Gamma\left(\kappa(1-\gamma)/2\gamma\right)+\log\Gamma\left(\kappa/2\gamma\right)-\frac{\kappa(1-\gamma)}{2\gamma}+\frac{\kappa}{2\gamma}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Define <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q(x):=x\psi(x)-\log\Gamma(x)-x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q(x):=x\psi(x)-\log\Gamma(x)-x</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, defining <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=\kappa(1-\gamma)/2\gamma,b=\kappa/2\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=\kappa(1-\gamma)/2\gamma,b=\kappa/2\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&lt;b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&lt;b</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that</span></p>
<table id="A5.EGx67" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex83"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex83.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\kappa^{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial\kappa}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=Q(a)-Q(b)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>κ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></munder><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\kappa^{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial\kappa}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=Q(a)-Q(b).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p6.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p6.3.1" class="ltx_text">Hence, to show that <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial}{\partial\kappa}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial}{\partial\kappa}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we only need to show that <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly increasing. We take the derivative</span></p>
<table id="A5.EGx68" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A5.Ex84"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex84.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle Q^{\prime}(x)=x\psi_{1}(x)-1." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>Q</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle Q^{\prime}(x)=x\psi_{1}(x)-1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p6.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p6.4.1" class="ltx_text">From <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al. (2015)</a></cite>, we get that <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi_{1}(x)&gt;1/(2x^{2})+1/x&gt;1/x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_{1}(x)&gt;1/(2x^{2})+1/x&gt;1/x</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence, <math id="A5.SS1.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{\prime}(x)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>Q</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{\prime}(x)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and we have the result.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Interestingly, this tells us how to reach the infimum of <math id="A5.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math>. We present the optimal joint infimum in the following corollary.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmcorollary1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmcorollary1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1</span></span><span id="Thmcorollary1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmcorollary1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmcorollary1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmcorollary1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The joint infimum, <math id="Thmcorollary1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\inf_{\kappa,\beta&gt;0}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>inf</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\inf_{\kappa,\beta&gt;0}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is reached for <math id="Thmcorollary1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=\beta^{*}(\kappa)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=\beta^{*}(\kappa)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmcorollary1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="Thmcorollary1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa,\beta\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa,\beta\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="Thmcorollary1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa/\beta=2\gamma/\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa/\beta=2\gamma/\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.5" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">For each <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, <a href="#Thmlemma9" title="Lemma 9 (Strict Convexity, Coercivity and Optimality of ℱ_∞^𝜆). ‣ E.1 Optimality of free energy under ratio ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> says that <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\arginf_{\beta&gt;0}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=\kappa\lambda/2\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>inf</mi></mrow><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">lim</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>λ</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>κ</mi><mi>λ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arginf_{\beta&gt;0}\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=\kappa\lambda/2\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>. Along this path, <a href="#Thmlemma10" title="Lemma 10. ‣ E.1 Optimality of free energy under ratio ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> gives us that <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly decreasing in <math id="A5.SS1.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, we have the result.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmremark4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 4</span></span><span id="Thmremark4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmremark4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">From <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3. ‣ 4.2 Limiting free energy ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and <a href="#Thmcorollary1" title="Corollary 1. ‣ E.1 Optimality of free energy under ratio ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, we see that the infimum of <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>lim</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{\tau\to 0}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> occurs for <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa,\beta\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa,\beta\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa/\beta\to 2\gamma/\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa/\beta\to 2\gamma/\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>. Under this limit, <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}\to\lambda^{-1}\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">HTMP</mtext><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">MP</mtext><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{HTMP}_{\gamma,\kappa,\beta}\to\lambda^{-1}\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>. Note however that <a href="#S3.Ex4" title="In 3.2 Evaluation of free energy using final-layer weights ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">BFE-
                              
                                W
                              
                            </span></a> was derived from models that interpolate the training data; for DNNs, <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">MP</mtext><mi>γ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to the spectrum of randomly initialized weights, which generally will <span id="Thmremark4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">not</span> interpolate complex training sets. Hence, <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">MP</mtext><mi>γ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> is mostly inaccessible for trained weights (at least for sufficiently complex learning tasks). Instead, for trained weights constrained to the interpolation manifold, <a href="#S3.Ex4" title="In 3.2 Evaluation of free energy using final-layer weights ‣ 3 Free energy for trained weights ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">BFE-
                              
                                W
                              
                            </span></a> prefers minimum distributional distance to <math id="Thmremark4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">MP</mtext><mi>γ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textbf{MP}_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Proof of Theorem 3.</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3. ‣ 4.2 Limiting free energy ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, we see that this result can be proved by combining <a href="#Thmlemma8" title="Lemma 8 (Increasing Shannon Transform). ‣ E.1 Optimality of free energy under ratio ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, <a href="#Thmlemma9" title="Lemma 9 (Strict Convexity, Coercivity and Optimality of ℱ_∞^𝜆). ‣ E.1 Optimality of free energy under ratio ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> and <a href="#Thmlemma10" title="Lemma 10. ‣ E.1 Optimality of free energy under ratio ‣ Appendix E Proofs for convexity and optimality of free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Proof of Lemma 1.</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the main text, we see that to fit the spectral distributions of trained weight matrices, often one can take <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\propto\tau^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\propto\tau^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, for proportionality constants that differ between models. Under this assumption, we can derive the optimal ratio. The result is given in <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1. ‣ 4.2 Limiting free energy ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, and we now give the proof.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1. ‣ 4.2 Limiting free energy ‣ 4 Heavy-tails and free energy ‣ Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\tau=c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\tau=c</annotation></semantics></math>, for some <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, the Tricomi term in <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}</annotation></semantics></math> no longer relies on <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence, for some <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>, we can take <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{\beta}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∂</mo><mi>β</mi></msub><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mi>λ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{\beta}\mathcal{F}_{\infty}^{\lambda}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Rearranging for <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h=\kappa/\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h=\kappa/\beta</annotation></semantics></math> gives the result.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.4 </span>Auxiliary lemma</h3>

<div id="A5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We require a result on the asymptotic expansion of ratios of Tricomi functions.</p>
